title: Learn File Servers and CDNs with S3 and CloudFront
description: Build secure upload, object-storage, streaming, caching, CDN, and recovery flows in Go.

lessons.title: Welcome
lessons.instruction: A file service manages bytes and metadata such as an object key, owner, media type, and size. Record the real byte size for the stored avatar.

lessons.title: Large Files
lessons.instruction: Stream large files through io.Reader and io.Writer instead of holding the whole upload in memory. Copy the first five bytes from the simulated upload.

lessons.title: Database
lessons.instruction: Keep searchable metadata in the database while object storage holds the bytes. Correct the row so it points to the uploaded MP4 and records its media type.

lessons.title: Videos
lessons.instruction: MP4 is a media container, while codecs describe how its tracks are encoded. Return the standard media type for an .mp4 response.

lessons.title: Multipart Uploads
lessons.instruction: Multipart boundaries separate regular form values from uploaded files. Read the file from the upload field and print its client filename; real handlers must also cap the request size.
lessons.starter:
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"mime/multipart"
	"net/http"
)

func main() {
	var body bytes.Buffer
	writer := multipart.NewWriter(&body)
	part, _ := writer.CreateFormFile("upload", "avatar.png")
	part.Write([]byte("png"))
	writer.Close()

	request, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/upload", &body)
	request.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
	request.ParseMultipartForm(1024)
	files := request.MultipartForm.File["file"]
	if len(files) == 0 {
		fmt.Println("missing")
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(files[0].Filename)
}
lessons.solution:

lessons.title: Encoding
lessons.instruction: Transcoding changes codec, bitrate, or resolution and is usually an asynchronous CPU-heavy job. Build the command arguments that encode the video with H.264.

lessons.title: Using the Filesystem
lessons.instruction: Local uploads must stay beneath a fixed root. Replace the traversal path with a safe relative path so cleaning and joining cannot escape /srv/uploads.

lessons.title: Mime Types
lessons.instruction: Do not trust a client-supplied filename or Content-Type. Inspect the first bytes of the payload and make the detector identify a PNG image.

lessons.title: Live Edits
lessons.instruction: Write edits to a temporary file and rename it atomically so readers never observe a partial file. Complete the replacement before reading the live path.
lessons.starter:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func main() {
	dir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "edit")
	defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
	live := filepath.Join(dir, "page.txt")
	temp := live + ".tmp"
	os.WriteFile(live, []byte("old"), 0600)
	os.WriteFile(temp, []byte("new"), 0600)
	data, _ := os.ReadFile(live)
	fmt.Println(string(data))
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func main() {
	dir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "edit")
	defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
	live := filepath.Join(dir, "page.txt")
	temp := live + ".tmp"
	os.WriteFile(live, []byte("old"), 0600)
	os.WriteFile(temp, []byte("new"), 0600)
	os.Rename(temp, live)
	data, _ := os.ReadFile(live)
	fmt.Println(string(data))
}

lessons.title: Caching
lessons.instruction: An ETag lets a client validate cached bytes without downloading them again. Match If-None-Match to the current ETag and return 304.

lessons.title: Cache Busting
lessons.instruction: A changed URL avoids stale shared caches more reliably than reusing the old asset path. Point the stylesheet at version v2.

lessons.title: Cache Headers
lessons.instruction: Cache-Control distinguishes shared public reuse from private or forbidden storage. Allow public caches to keep this versioned asset for one hour.

lessons.title: New Files
lessons.instruction: Versioned files can be cached as immutable because new bytes receive a new name. Publish the new logo under its release-specific path.

lessons.title: Single Machine
lessons.instruction: Local disk ties bytes to one host, so replacement and horizontal scaling can lose access to uploads. Choose the shared backend for three application replicas.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	replicas := 3
	backend := "local disk"
	fmt.Println(replicas, backend)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	replicas := 3
	backend := "shared object storage"
	fmt.Println(replicas, backend)
}

lessons.title: AWS
lessons.instruction: An S3 client needs a region and bucket, while credentials should come from the workload environment rather than source code. Correct the deployment configuration.

lessons.title: Serverless
lessons.instruction: Managed services remove server administration, not authorization or failure handling. Arrange a direct-upload flow so the API authorizes before signing and the browser uploads last.

lessons.title: Upload Object
lessons.instruction: S3 and MinIO PUT operations identify a bucket, opaque key, body, and useful metadata such as Content-Type. Complete the local request model for the PNG upload.

lessons.title: Architecture
lessons.instruction: A practical local stack mirrors production: the browser asks the API for authorization, MinIO stores S3-compatible objects, and a CDN serves cached responses. Put the components in request order.

lessons.title: SDKs and S3
lessons.instruction: An SDK handles request signing, transport, retries, and contexts; your code still owns safe keys and policy. Add a deadline to the simulated upload context.

lessons.title: Object Storage
lessons.instruction: MinIO provides an S3-compatible object store for local practice. Run Check to verify that its health endpoint is ready.
lessons.starter: check
lessons.expected: PASS · The live object-storage services are ready.

lessons.title: File System Illusion
lessons.instruction: Slashes are characters in an object key; consoles imitate folders by listing prefixes. Count the keys beneath users/42/ without assuming directories exist.

lessons.title: Dynamic Path
lessons.instruction: Object keys use slash semantics on every operating system. Build the validated user's avatar key with path.Join rather than filepath.Join.

lessons.title: Streaming
lessons.instruction: Byte-range delivery lets a player seek without downloading the whole file. Request bytes 2 through 5 and let http.ServeContent produce the partial response.
lessons.starter:
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	request := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/video", nil)
	request.Header.Set("Range", "bytes=0-1")
	response := httptest.NewRecorder()
	http.ServeContent(response, request, "video.bin", time.Unix(0, 0), bytes.NewReader([]byte("0123456789")))
	fmt.Println(response.Code, response.Body.String(), response.Header().Get("Content-Range"))
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	request := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/video", nil)
	request.Header.Set("Range", "bytes=2-5")
	response := httptest.NewRecorder()
	http.ServeContent(response, request, "video.bin", time.Unix(0, 0), bytes.NewReader([]byte("0123456789")))
	fmt.Println(response.Code, response.Body.String(), response.Header().Get("Content-Range"))
}

lessons.title: MP4
lessons.instruction: Fast-start MP4 places metadata before the media payload so playback can begin during download. Put the simplified moov atom before mdat.

lessons.title: More Requests
lessons.instruction: A valid Range response uses 206, includes Content-Range, and returns only the requested bytes. Make the requested inclusive interval exactly 100 bytes long.

lessons.title: Other Approaches
lessons.instruction: HLS and DASH split media into small segments and can adapt bitrate between requests. Replace the single-file delivery with an HLS playlist and segment.

lessons.title: Security
lessons.instruction: Treat upload names, sizes, declared types, and bytes as untrusted. Enforce the five-byte limit before an oversized body reaches storage.

lessons.title: Application vs. Developer
lessons.instruction: Developers should use managed human login, while deployed applications use workload roles with temporary credentials. Select the production credential source.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	environment := "production"
	credentialSource := "developer-access-key"
	fmt.Println(environment, credentialSource)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	environment := "production"
	credentialSource := "workload-role"
	fmt.Println(environment, credentialSource)
}

lessons.title: Scoping Permission
lessons.instruction: Least privilege limits both operations and resources, often to one object-key prefix. Allow this PUT only beneath users/42/.

lessons.title: Roles
lessons.instruction: A role supplies short-lived credentials that the platform rotates. Make the simulated credential remain valid after the fixed current time.

lessons.title: Private Bucket
lessons.instruction: Keep public access blocked and grant only the application or CDN origin identity permission to read. Correct the simplified bucket posture.

lessons.title: Signed URLs
lessons.instruction: A signed URL grants one method on one object until a short expiry; it is not general bucket access. Correct the permitted method for this unexpired download.

lessons.title: Encryption
lessons.instruction: TLS protects bytes in transit, while server-side encryption protects stored objects. Enable TLS and select the managed-key mode for data at rest; authorization is still required.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	inTransit := "plain HTTP"
	atRest := "none"
	fmt.Println(inTransit, atRest)
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	inTransit := "TLS"
	atRest := "aws:kms"
	fmt.Println(inTransit, atRest)
}

lessons.title: Regions
lessons.instruction: Region choice affects latency, residency, cost, and failure boundaries. Colocate this application's origin bucket with the application region.

lessons.title: CDNs
lessons.instruction: A CDN reuses an edge copy when the cache key matches and goes to the origin on a miss. Store each missed URL so repeated requests become hits.

lessons.title: Use CloudFront
lessons.instruction: A secure CloudFront distribution uses a private S3 origin, origin access control, and HTTPS-only viewer behavior. Correct the simplified distribution settings.

lessons.title: Invalidations
lessons.instruction: Invalidations propagate asynchronously and may cost money, so routine releases should use versioned URLs. Publish v3 without purging the old cached path.

lessons.title: Why CDNs?
lessons.instruction: Cache hits reduce viewer latency, origin bandwidth, and origin work. Raise the hit ratio to 80 percent and calculate how many of 1,000 requests reach the origin.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	requests := 1000
	hitPercent := 50
	origin := requests * (100 - hitPercent) / 100
	fmt.Println("origin requests:", origin)
}
lessons.solution:

import "fmt"

func main() {
	requests := 1000
	hitPercent := 80
	origin := requests * (100 - hitPercent) / 100
	fmt.Println("origin requests:", origin)
}

lessons.title: Availability
lessons.instruction: Availability measures whether the service can respond when requested. Use a 99.9 percent monthly target and calculate the whole minutes of allowed downtime in 30 days.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	monthMinutes := 30 * 24 * 60
	targetPerThousand := 990
	allowed := monthMinutes * (1000 - targetPerThousand) / 1000
	fmt.Println(allowed, "minutes")
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	monthMinutes := 30 * 24 * 60
	targetPerThousand := 999
	allowed := monthMinutes * (1000 - targetPerThousand) / 1000
	fmt.Println(allowed, "minutes")
}

lessons.title: Reliability
lessons.instruction: Reliability means sustained correct behavior. Retry only safe operations, cap the attempts, and back off between them; produce the three bounded delays.

lessons.title: Durability
lessons.instruction: Durability measures whether stored data remains intact, which differs from whether it is reachable now. Retain the object after one of three copies fails.

lessons.title: Bucket Versioning
lessons.instruction: Versioning preserves earlier object versions, while an ordinary delete adds a delete marker. Restore the newest stored value beneath that marker.

lessons.title: Delete
lessons.instruction: In a versioned bucket, deleting the current object adds a marker without erasing historical versions. Append the marker and report the resulting state.
